Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

either … or conjunction

classical

Cic. Tusc. 5.118: aut bibat, inquit, aut abeat
Publ. N 64: Nīl nōn aut lēnit aut domat diūturnitās.

aut … aut

conjunctions, before each member

One or the other, not both.

Other words

  • vel … vel — either … or (whichever you like)

    conjunctions, before each member · also used · classical · Gell. 1.15.10: vel utī taceat vel utī loquātur

    The choice is free, and both may hold.

Examples

  • aut bibat, inquit, aut abeat

    “let him either drink,” he says, “or go”Cic. Tusc. 5.118

  • aut librīs mē dēlectō … aut flūctūs numerō

    either I enjoy my books or I count the wavesCic. Att. 2.6.1

  • Nīl nōn aut lēnit aut domat diūturnitās.

    There is nothing that time does not either soften or tame.Publ. N 64

  • frustō … pānis condūcī potest, vel utī taceat vel utī loquātur

    he can be hired for a crust of bread, either to keep quiet or to talkGell. 1.15.10

See also or, whether … or, neither … nor, both … and.

SourcesLewis & Short: aut · Lewis & Short: vel
